title: RTX 5070 vs RTX 5080 in the US (2026) — which graphics card to buy
description: RTX 5070 vs RTX 5080 desktop graphics cards compared in the United States for 2026: how Blackwell architecture, 12GB vs 16GB VRAM, TBP and DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation change the upgrade math for Newegg, Best Buy, B&H, Amazon and Micro Center shoppers, with live USD prices from MSI, ASUS, ZOTAC, Gigabyte and PNY.

heroBody: NVIDIA's RTX 5070 and RTX 5080 desktop graphics cards sit one tier apart in the Blackwell 50-series lineup, and in the US in 2026 that gap decides whether you are spending close to the entry sticker for a strong 1440p card with 12GB of VRAM or stepping up to a meaningful premium for the same games at native 4K with frame generation on. The 5070 ships with 12GB of GDDR7 and is the sensible pick for 1080p and 1440p gaming with ray tracing; the 5080 doubles the VRAM to 16GB, opens up native 4K at high refresh, and pushes the ray-tracing budget meaningfully further. Both ship on MSI Gaming, MSI Ventus, MSI Shadow, ZOTAC Twin Edge, ASUS TUF and PNY boards at Newegg, Best Buy, B&H and Micro Center, but the price gap between a 5070 SKU and the equivalent 5080 SKU at the same retailer can be the difference between a value buy and a flagship buy. This page pulls the live US listings so you can see both floor prices side by side, and the comparison below lays out the meaningful differences so you can decide whether the 5080 premium is worth the money to you.

highlightSectionTitle: What actually changes between the RTX 5070 and RTX 5080 desktop

highlights.title: VRAM and the long tail of useful life
highlights.body: The single biggest difference for shoppers who keep a GPU for four or more years is VRAM. The 5070 ships with 12GB GDDR7 on a 192-bit bus; the 5080 ships with 16GB on a wider 256-bit bus. Several 2026 games already nudge past 8GB at high textures and path-traced settings, and a handful of flagship releases in late 2026 and into 2027 will land closer to 12GB. A 5070 is comfortable today but tighter by the end of its life; a 5080 buys meaningful headroom.

highlights.title: CUDA cores and raster frame rate
highlights.body: The 5080 has 10,752 CUDA cores versus 6,144 on the 5070 — roughly 75% more cores — and the gap shows up as a meaningful uplift in raster frame rate, especially at 1440p and 4K. If you play competitive esports at 1080p 240Hz you are CPU-bound on most titles and the difference is smaller; if you play modern AAA at native panel resolution, the 5080 pulls clearly ahead.

highlights.title: TBP and case cooling
highlights.body: The 5070 reference TBP is 250W and most custom boards ship between 220W and 300W. The 5080 reference TBP is 320W and most custom boards ship between 320W and 360W, with flagship AIO and triple-fan SKUs at the top end. The 5080 needs a quality 850W+ PSU and good case airflow; the 5070 is comfortable on a quality 650W unit. Always check the spec sheet on the product page — Newegg lists TBP clearly, marketplace listings often do not.

highlights.title: Ray tracing and DLSS 4 headroom
highlights.body: Both cards support DLSS 4 with Multi Frame Generation using the new Transformer model, but the 5080 has more raw compute to spend on the frame-generation budget. In path-traced titles the 5080 holds native panel refresh in scenes where a 5070 starts to dip. If you want full path tracing at 1440p with frame gen, the 5070 gets you there; at 4K with path tracing the 5080 is the card you actually want.

highlights.title: Power draw and noise
highlights.body: Because the 5080 ships at higher TBP, a 5080 build runs hotter and louder under load than a 5070 in the same case class. Idle power is similar. If your build is in a small form factor case or a quiet living-room tower, the 5070 is the kinder choice; if your build lives in a full tower with good airflow, the 5080's thermal headroom is a non-issue and the additional performance is right there.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pick in the US in 2026
advicePoints: Pick the RTX 5070 if you game at 1080p or 1440p, mostly play esports and modern AAA without path tracing on, and want the best performance-per-dollar in the 50-series desktop lineup. It is the smart US buy for most shoppers and the floor price on the live cards above is well under the 5080's typical premium.

Pick the RTX 5080 if you have a 1440p high-refresh or 4K panel, want full path tracing with DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation, or plan to keep the GPU for four or more years. The 16GB VRAM and CUDA core count both buy real headroom past the 5070.

Always check the TBP in the spec sheet, not just the model name. A '5070' at 220W is meaningfully slower than the same name at 300W; Newegg, B&H and Micro Center list TBP clearly, marketplace listings often do not.

Match the GPU to your monitor: a 1080p 240Hz screen pairs well with a 5070; a 1440p 240Hz or 4K 120Hz screen benefits from a 5080. Buying a 5080 to drive a 1080p 165Hz panel leaves performance on the table; buying a 5070 to drive a 4K 120Hz screen starves the display.

Time your buy around Amazon Prime Day (July), Labor Day hangover sales into early September 2026, Black Friday (late November), and Micro Center's in-store-only GPU drops. Outside those windows, Newegg and B&H typically hold the lowest everyday price on base board configurations.

Watch the Newegg Shuffle and Micro Center in-store only deals for high-end 5080 SKUs at meaningful discounts — they sell out within hours, so set a stock alert before the next drop. Online-only retailers rarely match these.

Avoid listings well below the market floor on eBay or unknown Amazon sellers — they are usually used, refurbished or mining cards dressed up as new. Buy from Newegg, B&H, Best Buy, Micro Center or Amazon-sold-by-NVIDIA to keep the manufacturer's US warranty intact.
faqSectionTitle: RTX 5070 vs RTX 5080 in the US — common questions

faqs.question: Is the RTX 5080 worth the premium over the RTX 5070 in the US?
faqs.answer: If you have a 1440p or 4K panel, want full path tracing, or plan to keep the GPU four or more years, yes — the 16GB VRAM and 75% more CUDA cores pay back over the useful life of the card. If you game at 1080p or 1440p without path tracing and plan to upgrade in three years, the 5070 is the smarter US buy and the floor price on the live cards above is well below the 5080's typical premium.

faqs.question: How much more expensive is the RTX 5080 than the 5070 in the US?
faqs.answer: Across the same board classes, a 5080 SKU typically sits 2x to 2.5x the price of an equivalent 5070 SKU. The live cards above show the current USD floor for 5070 boards; 5080 boards (MSI Gaming Trio, ASUS ROG Astral, ZOTAC AMP Extreme) typically land well above that band. The exact gap moves with the latest Newegg Shell Shuffle drops and Micro Center in-store promos.

faqs.question: Does the RTX 5080 support 4K gaming in the US?
faqs.answer: Yes — the 5080 with 16GB VRAM and DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation is comfortable at 4K high/ultra in most 2026 releases. The 5070 can also drive a 4K panel with DLSS, but you will see dips in path-traced scenes. If your monitor is 4K 120Hz or higher, the 5080 is the card that actually drives it well.

faqs.question: Should I wait for an RTX 5070 Ti or RTX 5080 Ti in the US?
faqs.answer: NVIDIA has not announced a 5070 Ti or 5080 Ti for the US desktop lineup at the time of writing. The current 50-series desktop stack in the US runs RTX 5070, RTX 5070 Ti (in select boards), RTX 5080 and RTX 5090. If you need a 50-series card today, buy the GPU that matches your workload from the options above; if you can wait, watch for any 5070 Ti refresh announcements and the next round of Newegg and Micro Center drops.

faqs.question: What power supply do I need for the RTX 5070 and RTX 5080 in the US?
faqs.answer: Most RTX 5070 boards run comfortably on a quality 650W PSU from a reputable brand (Corsair RM, Seasonic Focus, EVGA G7). The RTX 5080 wants a quality 850W unit, with the high-end AIO boards pushing toward 1000W for headroom. Cheap off-brand PSUs at the same wattage are a real risk on a 5080 build; spend the line item on a known brand.

faqs.question: Do RTX 5070 and 5080 graphics cards bought in the US come with manufacturer warranty?
faqs.answer: Boards bought from Newegg, B&H, Best Buy, Micro Center and Amazon-sold-by-NVIDIA carry the manufacturer's US warranty — typically three years for MSI, ASUS, ZOTAC, Gigabyte and PNY boards. eBay or unknown Amazon Marketplace sellers often ship with no US warranty or only a 30-day store return; check the listing language carefully before you click buy.

categoryIntro.heading: Why RTX 5070 and 5080 prices vary so much in the US
categoryIntro.body: The US 50-series desktop market is dominated by Newegg, Best Buy, B&H, Micro Center and Amazon, with MSI, ASUS, ZOTAC, Gigabyte and PNY shipping dozens of board variants at different TBP and cooler tiers. Most boards hold list price most of the year; the real discounts come from Amazon Prime Day, Black Friday, and Micro Center's in-store GPU drops. The same GPU can therefore carry very different price tags depending on the channel and the board, which is why the live cards on this page read straight from the catalog — a static 'cheapest RTX 5080' article goes stale within a week.
